newsitem.title: CHINA: China central bank chief warns of financial risk.
newsitem.headline: China central bank chief warns of financial risk.

text.p: China's central bank chief Dai Xianglong has warned that non-performing loans of state commercial banks were too high, the official Financial News reported on Tuesday.
Dai, governor of the People's Bank of China, was quoted as saying he did not see a financial crisis ahead but non-performing loans were contributing to financial risk in the nation's banking system.
Inadequate management of the securities markets and the operations of unlicensed financial institutions were also problems that needed to be addressed, he said.
Dai made the remarks at the annual meeting of the Bank for International Settlements in Basle, Switzerland.
China has been trying to keep bank funds out of the stock market to limit financial risk and volatility.
The People's Bank has increased its supervision of financial institutions and boosted internal controls, Dai said.
China's central bank has also attempted to control risk by maintaining an appropriately tight monetary policy and protecting the stability of the currency, Dai said.
